Electrical Safety & Standards

 Earth Leakage Relay: 7 Essential Steps for Safe LT Panels

 A large feeder can leak hundreds of milliamps to earth long before its breaker notices any overcurrent. An earth leakage relay watches that hidden residual current through a core balance CT and trips the breaker before the leak becomes a fire or a shock.

 
 CBCT Sensing 
 30 mA to 30 A 
 Time Delay 
 Shunt Trip 
 




 An earth leakage relay pairs a core balance current transformer with an adjustable relay to protect big LT feeders against earth leakage. This guide covers settings, wiring, testing and selection for Indian plants.


 
 Hello everyone, today we are going to learn how an earth leakage relay works with a CBCT, how to set its sensitivity and delay, and how to wire, test and select one.


 
 
 
 What Is an Earth Leakage Relay?


 An earth leakage relay, usually called an ELR, is a protective relay that measures the residual current of a circuit through a core balance current transformer (CBCT) and operates an output contact when that current exceeds a set value. The contact trips a breaker fitted with a shunt trip or undervoltage release, unlike an RCCB or ELCB that sense and break in one body.


 In a healthy circuit, the current going out on the phases returns on the phases and neutral, so the vector sum is zero. When insulation fails and some current flows to earth, the sum is no longer zero, and the CBCT produces a small secondary signal much like any current transformer does.


 
 
 Image credit: Rayleigh Instruments . Product photo courtesy of Rayleigh Instruments, shown here for educational reference.

 How an Earth Leakage Relay Works With a CBCT


 
 Conductors Pass Through All phases and neutral go through the CBCT window

 Fluxes Cancel Healthy load currents sum to zero

 Leak Appears Current returns through earth, flux remains

 Signal Measured Relay compares residual current with set value

 Delay Runs Selected time delay must expire

 Contact Changes Shunt trip opens the MCCB or ACB




 The CBCT is a toroid with many secondary turns, and the primary is simply the bundle of live conductors passing through it. Because the protective earth conductor must stay outside the window, the leakage current that returns through earth is exactly what the CBCT sees.


 Modern relays measure the true RMS value of this residual signal, compare it with the setting and start a timer. Rayleigh lists a response under 30 ms at five times the set point and under 50 ms at the set point for its RI ELR60.


 Do You Know?
 Rayleigh notes that IEC 60947 2 Annex M expects a failsafe output contact on such relays. The contact is held energised while healthy, so a lost auxiliary supply or broken coil also gives a trip or alarm.
